title: SDK Verification & Automation
description: Test strategy, harness design, coverage thinking, and automation leadership for SDKs

questions.question: You join as verification manager. The SDK has 8,000 tests, average runtime 14 hours, and no clear ownership. What is your first 30-day operating plan? (bullet the top 3 actions)
questions.modelAnswer:
1) Define critical smoke + ownership map
2) Measure flake rate / runtime hotspots
3) Establish quality SLOs and a triage rotation
questions.explanation: Leadership starts with signal, ownership, and a thin trustworthy gate — not rewriting everything.

questions.question: Which test pyramid layer should catch most SDK API contract regressions cheapest?
options: Fast unit/component tests close to the API boundary
Manual exploratory testing once per year
questions.explanation: Shift-left: cheap deterministic tests should own contract regressions; HW labs catch what they uniquely can.

questions.question: Write a pytest test that asserts function add(2, 3) == 5. Include the import if needed.
questions.explanation: pytest discovers test_* functions and uses assert.

questions.scenario: A new SDK feature exposes async completion events. Bugs escape as “hangs” in customer clusters.
questions.question: Design a verification idea that would catch hangs (what oracle / technique)?
questions.modelAnswer: Use timeouts/watchdogs plus progress oracles (event counts, heartbeat counters) under stress/concurrency — fail if no progress within bound.
questions.explanation: Hangs need liveness oracles, not only value assertions.

questions.question: Differentiate verification vs validation in one crisp sentence each.
questions.modelAnswer: Verification: build the product right vs the spec/design. Validation: build the right product vs user/needs.
questions.explanation: Classic V&V wording — useful in manager interviews.

questions.question: What is a good property of a scalable automation framework?
options: Stable APIs, parallel execution, clear fixtures, and actionable reporting
Hard-coded sleeps and absolute GUI coordinates everywhere
Single global mutable state shared by all tests
Password secrets committed into the repo for convenience
questions.explanation: Scalable harnesses optimize for reuse, isolation, parallelism, and debuggability.

questions.question: Write a small Python helper `retry(fn, attempts=3)` that calls fn until it succeeds or attempts are exhausted (re-raise last exception).
questions.explanation: Retries belong in helpers with limits — and should still surface failure.

questions.question: A vendor proposes 100% line coverage as the only exit criterion. How do you respond as verification lead?
questions.modelAnswer: Coverage is necessary but not sufficient — pair with risk-based scenarios, negative tests, and oracles; coverage without meaningful asserts is theater.
questions.explanation: Managers must push back on vanity metrics.

questions.scenario: API v2 must stay compatible with v1 clients for 12 months.
questions.question: Name two concrete automated checks you would add to protect compatibility.
questions.modelAnswer: Contract/schema tests against recorded v1 client traces, and a compatibility suite that runs v1 clients against v2 in CI.
questions.explanation: Compatibility needs executable contracts, not wiki promises.

questions.question: When should a test write to a shared lab device without locking?
options: Basically never — shared mutable hardware needs isolation or leases
questions.explanation: HW-in-loop farms require leases/mutexes/namespaces or you get heisenbugs.

questions.question: Using pytest, write a fixture named `client` that yields an object SdkClient() and closes it afterward (use yield).
questions.starterCode:
import pytest
from sdk import SdkClient
questions.explanation: yield fixtures setup/teardown cleanly — essential harness literacy.

questions.question: Invent a severity rubric line for a bug that corrupts data rarely but silently. What severity and why?
questions.modelAnswer: High/Critical — silent data corruption undermines trust even if rare; prioritize detectability and fixes.
questions.explanation: Silent corruption beats loud crashes in severity conversations.

followUpQuestions.question: Verification asks: did we build the product ____?
followUpQuestions.explanation: Verification ≈ build it right / to spec.

followUpQuestions.question: Minimal pytest assert that 1 + 1 equals 2 inside test_math.
Best place for most API contract tests?
options: Fast automated tests near the API
Only multi-week soak on rare hardware

followUpQuestions.question: Name one oracle useful for detecting hangs.
Why is line coverage alone a weak exit criterion?

tutorial.intro: Learn how strong verification teams think: oracles, harnesses, pytest mechanics, and metrics that measure trust — not vanity.

levels.title: Basics
levels.tagline: Verification vs validation, smoke gates, first pytest
levels.html:
• Verification: Did we build the product right (matches spec/design)?
  • Validation: Did we build the right product (matches user need)?
Why managers care

You can be 100% verified against a wrong spec. Validation catches “built the wrong thing.”

Your first pytest

pytest -q test_add.py
pytest
Test runner that discovers test_* functions/files.
-q
Quiet summary output.
test_add.py
File containing tests.
from sdkmath import add

def test_add():
    assert add(2, 3) == 5
  • def test_... — discovery naming convention.
  • assert — pytest rewrites asserts to show diffs on failure.
First 30 days as verification lead
  1. Define a tiny merge-blocking smoke with owners
  2. Measure flake % and runtime
  3. Map ownership before rewriting thousands of tests
pytest --collect-only -q
--collect-only
Show which tests would run without executing them — great for ownership/smoke scoping.
pytest -k smoke -q
-k smoke
Only run tests whose names match the expression “smoke”.

levels.title: Advanced
levels.html:
Oracles (how you know a test is meaningful)

  • Value oracle: output equals golden/expected.
  • Liveness oracle: progress/heartbeat within timeout (catches hangs).
  • Safety oracle: never observe duplicate commits / torn messages.
  • Metamorphic: transform input in a way that should preserve result.

pytest fixture with cleanup

import pytest
from sdk import SdkClient

@pytest.fixture
def client():
    c = SdkClient()
    yield c
    c.close()
  • @pytest.fixture — reusable setup object injected into tests by name.
  • yield — pause here while the test runs; code after yield is teardown.
  • c.close() — always release HW/sessions even if the test failed.

Retries with a limit

def retry(fn, attempts=3):
    last = None
    for _ in range(attempts):
        try:
            return fn()
        except Exception as e:
            last = e
    raise last
Coverage theater

Line coverage without strong oracles can be 100% and still miss hangs, races, and compatibility breaks.

Shared lab devices

Never write concurrent jobs to the same mutable device without a lease/lock. That is how you manufacture heisenbugs.

pytest -n auto --maxfail=5
-n auto
Parallelize via pytest-xdist using CPU count (install pytest-xdist).
--maxfail=5
Stop after 5 failures — fail fast in CI.
Parametrize

One test function × many MTUs/offload modes beats copy-pasted tests. Use @pytest.mark.parametrize.

levels.title: Expert
levels.html:
• Keep v1 clients in CI against v2 SDK (contract/schema + behavioral suite).
  • Silent data corruption ⇒ high/critical even if rare.
  • Scale metrics: wall-clock, flake %, parallel efficiency, MTTR, % tests with owners.
Pushback line

“Coverage is necessary but not sufficient — here is the risk-based scenario set that protects customers.”

pytest --junitxml=reports/junit.xml
--junitxml=...
Write machine-readable results for Jenkins/GitHub to display.
